title: Curved Steel Armature for a Sauropod Dinosaur Tail

instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Curved Steel Armature for a Sauropod Dinosaur Tail
summary: Analyze a circular-arc museum armature under a linearly decreasing distributed gravity load using equilibrium, local section resultants, and a slender-member combined-stress approximation.
imageAlt: Museum gallery containing mounted dinosaur skeletons; the elevated tail provides application context only.

problemStatement:
A museum engineering team must conceal a curved steel support within an elevated sauropod tail. Model the support centerline as a circular arc of radius {{curved_tail_R_m}} m from the fixed root at θ = 0 to θt = {{curved_tail_theta_t_rad}} rad. Analyze section S at θS = {{curved_tail_theta_S_rad}} rad.

The total downward gravity load intensity, defined per meter of arc length, decreases linearly from {{curved_tail_q0_N_m}} N/m at the root to {{curved_tail_qt_N_m}} N/m at the tip. It already includes armature self-weight, so do not add self-weight again. The assigned section is {{curved_tail_H_mm}} × {{curved_tail_B_mm}} × {{curved_tail_tnom_mm}} mm nominal with design thickness t = {{curved_tail_t_factor}}tnom. These geometry and load values are instructional assumptions, not measurements from the photograph or verified product data.
engineeringGoal: Use curved-centerline equilibrium to determine fixed-root reactions and local axial force, shear force, and bending moment at S. Apply a slender-member straight-beam stress approximation to check combined longitudinal normal stress against the assigned yield criterion and explain what remains outside the model.
